Escape unicode characters in ASCII content, for example convert `"` to `“`.

Add `dirty="0"` to `<a:rPr>` and `<a:endParaRPr>` elements to indicate a clean state.

When adding a new slide to the end of the presentation, create the slide file `ppt/slides/slideN.xml`.
When adding a new slide, update `[Content_Types].xml` with an Override for the new slide.
When adding a new slide, update `ppt/_rels/presentation.xml.rels` with a relationship for the new slide.
When adding a new slide, update `ppt/presentation.xml` by adding a slide ID to `<p:sldIdLst>`.
When adding a new slide, create slide relationships in `ppt/slides/_rels/slideN.xml.rels` if needed.
When adding a new slide, update `docProps/app.xml` by incrementing the slide count and updating statistics if present.
When duplicating a slide, copy the source slide XML file with a new name.
When duplicating a slide, update all IDs in the new slide to be unique.
When duplicating a slide, follow the 'Adding a New Slide' steps.
When duplicating a slide, remove or update any notes slide references in `_rels` files.
When duplicating a slide, remove references to unused media files.
When reordering slides, update `ppt/presentation.xml` by reordering `<p:sldId>` elements in `<p:sldIdLst>`.
When reordering slides, keep slide IDs and relationship IDs unchanged.
When deleting a slide, remove the `<p:sldId>` entry from `ppt/presentation.xml`.
When deleting a slide, delete the relationship from `ppt/_rels/presentation.xml.rels`.
When deleting a slide, delete the Override entry from `[Content_Types].xml`.
When deleting a slide, delete the files `ppt/slides/slideN.xml` and `ppt/slides/_rels/slideN.xml.rels`.
When deleting a slide, update `docProps/app.xml` by decrementing the slide count and updating statistics.
When deleting a slide, clean up unused media by removing orphaned images from `ppt/media/`.

Before packing, fix `Content_Types.xml` to declare ALL slides, layouts, and themes present in the package.
Before packing, fix relationship IDs by removing font embed references if not using embedded fonts.
Before packing, remove broken references by checking all `_rels` files for references to deleted resources.

Never use manual bullet symbols (•, -, *) in HTML slides; use <ul> or <ol> lists instead.

Only use web-safe fonts in HTML slides: Arial, Helvetica, Times New Roman, Georgia, Courier New, Verdana, Tahoma, Trebuchet MS, Impact, Comic Sans MS; avoid custom fonts like Segoe UI, SF Pro, Roboto.
Use display: flex on the body element in HTML slides to prevent margin collapse from breaking overflow validation.
Use margin for spacing in HTML slides, noting that padding is included in size.

For inline formatting in HTML slides, use <b>, <i>, <u> tags or <span> with CSS styles supporting font-weight: bold, font-style: italic, text-decoration: underline, and color: #rrggbb; do not use margin or padding in <span> styles.
Use hex colors with # prefix in CSS for HTML slides.
Use CSS text-align (center, right, etc.) in HTML slides as a hint to PptxGenJS for text formatting if text lengths are slightly off.

For <div> elements in HTML slides, use CSS background or background-color to create shapes with backgrounds.

For <div> elements in HTML slides, use CSS border for uniform borders (e.g., border: 2px solid #333333) or partial borders (border-left, border-right, border-top, border-bottom) which render as line shapes.

For <div> elements in HTML slides, use CSS border-radius for rounded corners; border-radius: 50% or higher creates circular shapes, percentages <50% are calculated relative to the shape's smaller dimension, and px and pt units are supported.
For <div> elements in HTML slides, use CSS box-shadow for outer shadows only; inset shadows are ignored to prevent corruption.
Never use CSS gradients (linear-gradient, radial-gradient) in HTML slides as they don't convert to PowerPoint.
Always create gradient/icon PNGs first using Sharp, then reference them in HTML; rasterize SVG to PNG for gradients and rasterize react-icons SVG to PNG for icons.
Rasterize icons with Sharp by creating a function that renders the icon component to static markup, converts the SVG to PNG using sharp, and saves it to a file.
Rasterize gradients with Sharp by creating a function that generates an SVG with a linearGradient, converts it to PNG using sharp, and saves it to a file.
When using the html2pptx library, set the PptxGenJS layout to match the HTML body dimensions (e.g., pptx.layout = 'LAYOUT_16x9').
Call html2pptx with the HTML file path and the PptxGenJS presentation instance, and optionally provide options for tmpDir and slide.
After calling html2pptx, use the returned placeholders array to add charts to placeholder areas; find placeholders by ID if needed.
Add charts to placeholder positions using slide.addChart with the appropriate chart type and data.
When adding charts with PptxGenJS, never use # prefix with hex colors; use colors like 'FF0000' or '0066CC' to avoid file corruption.
When adding images with PptxGenJS, calculate aspect ratios from actual image dimensions and use them to set width and height.
When adding text with PptxGenJS, use rich text arrays with options for bold, italic, etc.
When adding shapes with PptxGenJS, use pptx.shapes.RECTANGLE, pptx.shapes.OVAL, or pptx.shapes.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE with appropriate fill, line, and rectRadius options.
When adding bar or line charts with PptxGenJS, include axis labels using catAxisTitle (category) and valAxisTitle (value).
For chart data, use single series with all labels for simple bar/line charts; each series creates a separate legend entry.

For time series data, choose the correct granularity: use daily grouping for < 30 days, monthly grouping for 30-365 days, and yearly grouping for > 365 days; validate that charts don't have only 1 data point.
For bar charts, set barDir to 'col' for vertical bars or 'bar' for horizontal bars, and use chartColors with a single color for single-series charts.
For scatter charts, prepare data with the first series containing X-axis values and subsequent series containing Y-values only.
For line charts, set lineSize, lineSmooth, and optionally valAxisMinVal, valAxisMaxVal, valAxisMajorUnit, and chartColors.
For pie charts, use a single data series with all categories in the labels array and corresponding values in the values array; no axis labels are required.
For multiple data series charts, provide an array of series objects each with name, labels, and values.
Align chart colors with the design palette, ensuring sufficient contrast and distinctiveness; avoid red-green only combinations for accessibility.
When adding tables with PptxGenJS, use slide.addTable with an array of rows, and set options like x, y, w, h, border, fill, align, valign, fontSize, colW, rowH, and autoPage.
For tables with custom formatting, use cell objects with text and options for fill, color, bold, colspan, etc.
For tables with merged cells, use colspan in cell options to merge cells across columns.
When creating a presentation, set pptx.author and pptx.title before adding slides.
Save the presentation using pptx.writeFile with a filename or options object.
Handle errors in the presentation creation process using .catch(console.error) or try-catch blocks.
